## v0.8.0
> ## ⚠️ Upgrading From 0.7.x: Read This First > > **This is a new OpenUsage. You have to add your accounts again.** Open the **Accounts** screen and sign in to each one. OpenUsage no longer picks up the sign-ins of the coding tools on your Mac, so most accounts don't carry over. > > **What carries over** > - The OpenRouter and Z.ai keys you saved in 0.7.x are added for you, unless you had turned that provider off. > - Your hidden metrics, metric order, and provider order apply to the first account you add for each provider. > > **What is gone** > - Spend and token estimates from local logs and model pricing. The app shows only what each provider's API reports for the accounts you sign in to. > - Account discovery. OpenUsage no longer reads other tools' credentials, config files, Keychain items, databases, or logs. > - iCloud sync of usage history, the local HTTP API, the log file, the Pi provider, and menu-bar stars. > > **If you script the `openusage` command:** the JSON changed. `providers` is keyed by account id (`codex@1a2b3c4d`), not by provider, and `schema` is now `openusage.limits.v2`. > > Background and discussion: [#1441](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1441)

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.7
item.description:
### Changed - Limit Resets now names each reset (Session, Weekly, Fable or Full Reset) and shows when to use it by. Claude, ChatGPT and Z.ai list their resets the same way, and **Use** spends the reset you picked. - Reset countdowns a month or more away read in months and days, like `3m 12d`, instead of `119d 12h`. - **⌘R** rereads every CLIProxyAPI hub's login list first, so a login turned off on the hub disappears instead of failing with "no working sign-in". - A hub's "logins OpenUsage doesn't support yet" count leaves out logins turned off on the hub and files that aren't logins. - Priority and All Usage switch as soon as you press a tab, with no sliding, and the **Next update** footer no longer flashes the new tab's rows behind it while the panel resizes. Reported by [@Atchferox](https://github.com/Atchferox) ([#1574](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1574#issuecomment-6737337990)).
### Fixed - Antigravity's Gemini limits match what Antigravity shows, and a lightly used session keeps its reset countdown instead of reading as untouched ([#1641](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/pull/1641)).

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.6
item.description:
### Added - Right-click a usage row on All Usage or Priority and choose **Hide** to turn it off, the same as its switch on the account's page. Requested by [@maddada](https://x.com/maddada) on X.
### Fixed - With **Always Show In Menu Bar** on, the `+N` count in the menu bar no longer counts Used Up limits.

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.5
item.description: ### Fixed - The "Notifications are off" note in Settings opens OpenUsage's page in System Settings → Notifications in one click ([#1617](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/pull/1617)). - In clock mode, a reset a few days out, like `Tue, 2:30 AM`, no longer runs into the percentage beside it. The reset column is now wide enough for an English day and time ([#1627](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1627)).

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.4
item.description:
### Changed - **Always Show In Menu Bar** under **Settings → Display → Priority** lists everything Priority does in the menu bar, in its order: Pinned, Running Out, Use It or Lose It, then Used Up. Off by default. **Show In Menu Bar** is now **Max Items In Menu Bar** ([#1611](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1611)). - Screen and account page slides run at the Mac's native 0.25 s pace, and switching between Priority and All Usage shows the new tab at once ([#1574](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1574#issuecomment-6652210093)). - **Hide From Screen Share** is now **Privacy Mode**, and also blurs account names in the panel while your screen is shared or recorded. While it's on, copied usage pictures blur every account name ([#1599](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/pull/1599)).
### Fixed - On macOS 26, rows scrolled under the panel's footer are frosted, as on macOS 15, so the footer stays readable ([#1619](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1619)). - A reset a few days out shows its minutes in clock mode, like `mié, 8:31`, so in a 24-hour locale its hour no longer reads like a day of the month ([#1613](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1613)).

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.3
item.description:
### Added - **Use It or Lose It** under **Settings → Display → Priority** lists a weekly or monthly limit that resets within 24 hours with over 50% left in its own Priority section, soonest reset first, with when it resets. It uses the same rule as the alert and stays out of the menu bar. On by default. - Copilot signs in on your company's GitHub Enterprise domain on GHE.com: leave the new Domain step blank for github.com, or enter an address like `octocorp.ghe.com` ([#1602](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1602)). - **Pace marks** are back, answering the pace marks request in [#1574](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1574#issuecomment-6634518518): with **Settings → Display → Pace Marks** on, a tick on each All Usage bar and Priority ring shows where usage would be at an even pace through the window. Off by default.
### Changed - **Settings → Display** puts Priority Icons and Priority Limits under one **Priority** heading. - Settings explains each setting in an ⓘ tooltip beside its name instead of a second line, and the Warning and Critical alerts now read "Alert when a limit requires your attention" and "Alert when a limit drops critically low". - Priority always lists **Used Up** last. - The panel footer shows the OpenUsage version again, over **Next update in …**, as in 0.7. - The usage history popover's empty message wraps onto lines of even width. - All Usage shows a provider's copy button beside its logo while the pointer is anywhere over its card, instead of in place of the logo.

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.2
item.description:
### Added - Z.ai accounts show a **Limit Resets** row for banked resets. Its details list Session and Weekly resets apart, earliest first, and **Use** spends the earliest of a window ([#1427](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1427)). - Muse Code provider: sign in with a Meta device code to see your subscription's Session and Weekly limits. - **Settings → Display → Priority Limits** sets how much left turns a limit Warning (orange) or Critical (red), for the colors, Running Out, the menu bar, and the alerts. The alerts are now named Warning and Critical. - **Burning Fast** under Priority Limits lists a limit that would run out before it resets at your current pace, however much it has left, under Running Out and in the menu bar, with when it would run out ([#1574](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1574)). On by default. - **Use It or Lose It** notification: a weekly or monthly limit resets within 24 hours with over 50% left ([#1593](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1593)). Off by default.
### Changed - Priority: a pinned limit or balance that's used up moves to **Used Up** until it resets, instead of staying under **Pinned** as an empty ring. - **Settings → General → Global Shortcut** uses the standard macOS shortcut recorder, and a usage range with no data shows the provider's mark gently pulsing instead of breathing rings.
### Fixed - Claude's Extra Usage shows the account's billing currency, such as €, instead of always $ ([#1425](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1425)). - Cursor: Extra Usage reads "Team Spend" when its limit is the team's shared pool, so it no longer looks like a personal cap. Personal limits still read Extra Usage. - Claude: Extra Usage reads "Spend" on an Enterprise plan, where it is the whole monthly bill ([#1260](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1260)).

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.1
item.description:
**Upgrading from 0.7.x:** add your accounts again from the **Accounts** screen. OpenUsage no longer picks up the sign-ins of the coding tools on your Mac, so most accounts don't carry over. The OpenRouter and Z.ai keys you saved in 0.7.x are added for you, unless you had turned that provider off.
The new OpenUsage announced in [#1441](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1441). The app shows only what each provider's API reports for the accounts you sign in to.
### Removed - Account discovery. OpenUsage no longer reads other tools' credentials, config files, Keychain items, databases, or logs. Sign in to each account from the new **Accounts** screen instead. - Spend and token estimates from local logs, model pricing, and the pricing supplement. The dashboard shows the limits and dollar values a provider reports, nothing computed apart from ChatGPT's credit value (below). - iCloud sync of usage history (daily tokens and spend). - The log file. The app logs through unified logging only (`log stream --predicate 'subsystem == "OpenUsage"'`). - The local HTTP API. - The Pi provider, which has no account sign-in. - The welcome screen, provider enable/disable switches, and the On Demand metric tier. - Menu-bar stars. The menu bar picks its own limits. - The Density setting and Reset All Customization. - OpenRouter's Credits bar, which measured spend against every credit ever bought, not a limit. Balance still shows what's left. - The Icon Style, Increase Transparency, Always Show Pacing, and Reduce Animations settings. Animations follow macOS's Reduce Motion setting.
### Changed - Dashboard: Today, Yesterday, and every other time range always show, at 0 when the provider reports nothing for them. An account's page still hides any of them with its switch. - Dashboard: balances always show, even at $0, including Cursor Credits when Cursor reports none. Extra Usage shows only while the provider has it on, even at $0, and hides while it is off: Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot, and Grok, whose "Disabled" row is gone. - Share: every share image ends with a tinted OpenUsage footer reading "Your AI Limits at a Glance", in place of the "Monitor Your AI Subscriptions with OpenUsage" line. - Panel: content scrolls cleanly under the top bar, with no glass backdrop, and blurs softly under the bottom bar only while something is under it. The account name in an account page's header fades its hover highlight in. - Z.ai: a key Z.ai refuses reads as rejected, not as an invalid response, so the 0.7.x key import stops checking it on every launch. - Dashboard: after an update from 0.7.x, the empty dashboard welcomes you back, says OpenUsage no longer reads your local accounts automatically, and asks you to add back the ones to track. - Accounts: add several accounts per provider, rename them, and remove them from the app. - Accounts: replace an API-key account's key from its page. A key, added or replaced, is saved only once a usage read accepts it. - Accounts: an account's page lists its metrics, each with a switch that hides it everywhere and a handle that drags it into order. - Accounts: once **Sign In Again** works, the sign-in closes and the panel opens on your Default Tab. - Accounts: **Sign In Again** shows on an account's page only while Priority lists it under Needs Attention. - Dashboard: cards per provider with a section per account. Drag to reorder and press ⌘Z to undo; right-click menus hold refresh, share screenshot, and quick links. - Dashboard: two tabs, **Priority** for the limits running out or used up, most urgent first, and **All Usage** for every account. The panel opens on the **Default Tab** in Settings, Priority at first. - Priority: pin a metric with the pin beside its switch on its account's page, and it gets a **Pinned** section at the top of Priority. While a pinned metric is running out, it shows under **Running Out** instead, never in both. - Priority: right-click a metric on All Usage or a row on Priority to **Pin** or **Unpin** it, and **All Clear** is always one row under the **Running Out** header. - Dashboard: an account that hasn't reported yet shows grey placeholder rows on Priority and All Usage instead of **Waiting for Usage**, even while other accounts have reported. - Priority: an account lists under **Needs Attention** only once a refresh fails, not while it loads on launch. - Menu bar: shows the limits closest to running out on its own. **Show In Menu Bar**, under Settings → Display → Priority Icons at the top of the tab, sets how many, from App Icon Only to Up to 5. It starts at Up to 3. - Menu bar: when an update is available, the app icon shows at the far right with a dot, after the limits and any `+7` count, whatever **Show In Menu Bar** is set to. - Notifications: Cutting It Close now fires when a limit drops under 30% left, not when its pace nears the limit. A switch you turned on in 0.7.x stays on. - Settings: **Log Level** is back under Advanced → Debug and keeps the level you chose in 0.7.x. It starts at Info and sets how much the app writes to the macOS log; Debug works in released builds too. - Severity colours are blue, orange, and red. - Codex accounts are shown as ChatGPT. The provider id the command line takes stays `codex`. - Breaking from 0.7.x: the `openusage` JSON keys `providers` by account id (`codex@1a2b3c4d`), not by provider (`.providers.codex`); `openusage codex | jq '.providers[]'` reads every ChatGPT account. `displayName` names the account the way the app does (`ChatGPT · Work`). `schema` is now `openusage.limits.v2`, so a script can tell this shape from 0.7.x's `v1`. The `errors` key is gone: the command no longer refreshes, and an account shows `"stale": true` once its last fetch is past `expiresAt`. `expiresAt`, the moment an account turns stale, is 10 minutes after `fetchedAt` instead of 5, when the app shows its clock next to the account. Exit code `4` now means nothing has been fetched yet for the named accounts, not that a refresh failed. ChatGPT's `creditValue` resource is gone; `credits` still reports the credit count. Copilot's `orgCredits` and `orgSpend` moved to an organization account; a personal account no longer reports them. - New app icon. - Claude: when Anthropic rate-limits a login, every card on it waits out the limit, across a relaunch too, and cards signed in to one login share one usage request. - A provider's `Retry-After` wait is honored up to an hour; a longer one is cut to an hour. - A provider number too large for the app, such as a window length, count, or credit balance, no longer crashes it: the value is treated as malformed. A reset that far off shows the longest countdown. - Sign-ins: an outage, a rate limit, or a lost connection while renewing a sign-in no longer reads as an expired sign-in. The refresh is tried again later, and a token that still works stays in use. - Sign-ins: a renewed sign-in the Keychain refuses to save stays in use and is saved on the next refresh, so the account no longer has to be added again. - OpenRouter: a Management key shows Balance and what the standard keys in your default workspace spent today, this week, and this month. A standard key shows its own spend and Key Limit. - OpenRouter: a Management key scoped to one workspace can be added. It shows that workspace's spend, without Balance, which OpenRouter keeps from workspace keys. - OpenRouter: a Management key adds Yesterday and Prior 30 Days from OpenRouter's activity. Resting the pointer on a range shows its BYOK spend, tokens, and top models. A standard key adds Budget and Free Requests. - OpenRouter: Today, This Week, and This Month no longer show the BYOK an earlier build saved. BYOK shows only when resting the pointer on a range. - Accounts: a new Cursor account is named after its email, not "Cursor Account". - Accounts: every account has a name the card shows. A blank name, or one that only repeats the provider's, becomes `<Provider> Account`, such as `OpenRouter Account`, for existing accounts too. - Provider responses are no longer saved to a cache under `~/Library/Caches`. The last fetched usage is saved on this Mac in the app's own preferences, with account names and the layout. - Accounts: a new Ollama account is named after its ollama.com email, not "Ollama". - Claude: the plan reads Max or Ultra, Anthropic's new names for Max 5x and Max 20x. - Cursor: Today, Yesterday, and Last 30 Days add the tokens Cursor reports, and resting the pointer on a range shows what Cursor reported for it: the charge, usage events, each kind of token, and the top models. - Dashboard: resting the pointer on a range with nothing but a zero total says `<Provider> didn't report any data for this range.`, for every provider. - Ollama: new Today, Yesterday, and Last 30 Days rows show the usage value and tokens Ollama reports for each UTC day, a Requests row counts the last 30 days' requests, and resting the pointer on a range shows what Ollama reported for it: requests, each kind of token, and the top models. - ChatGPT: Today, Yesterday, and Last 30 Days show the tokens counted on UTC days, and Credit Limit shows a workspace's spending limit. Resting the pointer on a range shows what ChatGPT reported for it. - Grok: a new sign-in no longer asks for `profile` or `api:access`, so its token can't run Grok models. Add the account again to drop them from an existing sign-in. - Accounts: connect a CLIProxyAPI server with its address and management key, and its Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Devin, and Grok logins show as accounts, kept in step with the server. A login you also signed in directly shows twice; the hub's copy carries the CLIProxyAPI mark. - Accounts: each CLIProxyAPI hub is one row under your accounts. Its page lists the accounts it mirrors and holds Replace Management Key… and Remove Hub…. You can connect more than one hub. On hub and account pages, the replace-key and remove actions sit together in one card. - CLIProxyAPI: a hub on Tailscale connects over http, the Connect sheet shows one message at a time, and it says when a hub doesn't use https. - Panel: it is exactly as tall as its content, with no empty space under a short list, and its top edge no longer jumps while it resizes. On macOS 15 it grows with the slide back from Accounts, not after it. - Accounts: accounts keep one order on every screen, grouped by provider, and an account keeps its place when another account of its provider is removed. - Accounts: a saved account this build can't read no longer hides the others, and it is kept as it was. - Accounts: renaming an account keeps ⌘Z undo for the layout. Hiding every metric shows a line pointing to Accounts, not the Add an Account screen. - Accounts: replacing a key that was waiting out a rate limit reads the new key at once. - Copilot: an organization account's right-click menu opens its **Organization Billing** page. - Sign-ins: Claude and Antigravity send a random `state`, never the PKCE verifier. A pasted Devin token is masked. - Sign-ins: a stray request to the sign-in callback, or a network error during a device-code sign-in, no longer ends the sign-in. - Sign-ins: a Claude sign-in whose profile can't be read fails with **Try Again** instead of adding an account with no identity, and **Sign In Again** always checks the new sign-in with its own request. - Antigravity: a refused token is renewed once, as in 0.7.16, and a failed project lookup is tried again on the next refresh instead of reading as an expired sign-in. - Refresh: one stuck read no longer stalls every refresh and notification. - Rate limits: a manual refresh, an early sign-in renewal, and a Claude request that finishes late all respect the provider's newest rate-limit wait. Copilot reads GitHub's rate-limit 403 as a rate limit, not a rejected token, and Antigravity keeps the wait when both of its hosts answer 429. - Claude: once a reset spends a grant's last reset, a reset left on another grant can be claimed without waiting for the next hourly check. - Cursor: a usage event without tokens adds 0 tokens, so it no longer hides its range's token total. - Notifications: Settings reads the notification permission from macOS each time, so a permission turned off in System Settings shows as off.
### Kept - Automatic updates through Sparkle, with the same release feed, the beta channel, and the update banner. - **Check for Updates…** in the dashboard's **⋯** menu, between Settings and Report an Issue…, as in 0.7.x. The dev build shows it and the Settings Updates section disabled instead of hiding them. - Anonymous telemetry through PostHog, with the same opt-out in Settings for extra analytics. An anonymous daily active ping and crash reports are always sent; they are not optional. - Notifications, keyboard shortcuts, Launch at Login, Theme, and Time Format. - The Almost Out, Cutting It Close, and Will Run Out switches in Settings, named after the alerts they send. A line under each says when it fires, in place of 0.7.x's info button. - The proxy setting in `~/.openusage/config.json`, which now covers sign-in too and logs an error when the file is invalid. - Your 0.7.x hidden metrics, metric order, and provider order, on the first account you add for each provider, from the account 0.7.x had on. Stars don't carry over. 0.7.x's saved layout stays on disk unchanged, so a downgrade finds it as it was. - The OpenRouter and Z.ai keys you typed into 0.7.x, added once as accounts on the first launch when the provider has no account yet, 0.7.x had it on, and the key still passes a usage read. A key that couldn't be checked or saved is tried again on the next launch. The key files stay unchanged. - Hide From Screen Share, which shows the app icon in the menu bar instead of usage while the screen is shared or recorded. - ChatGPT's Extra Usage row shows the credits' dollar value, an estimate at 4¢ a credit. - Copilot Org Credits and Org Spend, now on an organization account added with an owner's or billing manager's token. - The `openusage` command, which now prints what the app last fetched and nothing computed. `--force` is accepted and does nothing. - OpenRouter's **Credits** quick link, after Status Page and Usage Dashboard. - Ollama's and Z.ai's **API Keys** quick link, after Usage Dashboard. - Z.ai's notice when a key has no GLM Coding Plan. - Claude's Extra Usage reads like `$12.34 spent` when the account sets no monthly limit. - A Grok team account's plan, shown beside the notice that the account has no personal quota. - Cursor Enterprise and Team seats that Cursor's plan endpoint reports as Pro keep their Enterprise or Team label, Extra Usage, and request-based usage. The membership now comes from Cursor's `usage-summary`, read once an hour, not from Cursor's local database. - Cursor's Today, Yesterday, and Last 30 Days rows, now the dollars Cursor reports it charged for on-demand usage. Usage your plan includes counts as $0, and the Usage Trend chart is gone. - Devin's Daily, Weekly, and Extra Usage rows. Sign in on windsurf.com and paste the token it shows, or paste a Windsurf API key. - Claiming a Claude or ChatGPT rate-limit reset refreshes that account right away, so its meters and Limit Resets count update as soon as the result shows.
